messages:
sam_infra: Heads up — seeing ~22% of west1 GPU nodes fail to join after last night's BMC firmware rollout. OOB console shows 'Boot override: Enabled' and nodes never proceed to boot. Autoscaler marks them unhealthy and starts shedding pods.
deploy-bot: Rollout complete: bmc-fw-v1.2.3 -> west1 (finished 2024-11-01T23:04:00Z).
maya_oncall: ugh. any sign secureboot toggled or keys rotated by the fw? :thinking_face:
sam_infra: not seeing key rotation. SecureBoot flag appears unchanged, but Boot Override stays stuck in the OOB UI. IPMI toggles don't clear it. Warmboot attempts hit our ratecap quickly.
liam_sre: Can you paste the ipmitool chassis bootparam output for one of the stuck hosts?
sam_infra: pulling one off the pool now — output below.
```
# ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.12.34.56 -U redwood-admin -P **** chassis bootparam get 5
Boot Flag Valid         : yes
Boot Device Selector    : 3 (PXE)
Boot Info Acknowledge   : 0x00
Boot Initiator          : 0x02
Boot Override           : Enabled
```
liam_sre: hmm. Boot Override Enabled but Boot Info Acknowledge is 0x00 — indicates BMC thinks a manual override is active but host never cleared it. Vendor notes mention a race where BMC resets during attribute apply.
jordan_hw: vendor firmware release notes have a known issue: if BMC reboot occurs during NVRAM write the BootOverride bit can get stuck until a full power cycle + NVRAM rebuild. They've got a qa patch in v1.2.4 but it's not released to customers yet.
maya_oncall: can we mitigate without mass power cycling? That's going to cause ~4h of disruption for running workloads.
sam_infra: tried ipmi raw to clear override (`ipmitool raw 0x0c 0x38 0x01 0x00`), nothing. Tried toggling boot params then a soft-reset — still stuck. Warmbooting repeatedly triggers our BMC ratecap and then vendor drops SOL sessions.
liam_sre: Workaround suggestion: vendor support recommended sequence: 1) AC power cycle (chassis control) twice, 2) wait 30s for NVRAM shadow rebuild, 3) run `ipmitool chassis bootdev disk` to force boot device and clear override. It's manual and slow.
jordan_hw: also note: some racks have remote PDU chains that take ~45s to reinitialize, so double-cycle spacing matters. We'll coordinate with facilities if we go that route.
maya_oncall: can we throttle autoscaler so it doesn't shed jobs during manual remediation? Current shed rules drop pods at 5 nodes/min which will cause customer impact.
sam_infra: I've patched the cluster-autoscaler policy for west1 to set min-unavailable=0 for GPUs and disabled aggressive eviction for 30m. Manual scale-out initiated to buffer capacity.
ops-bot: alert: west1-gpu-pool available capacity -18% (estimated 120 of 680 GPUs offline). Pod eviction rate increased x3 since 23:15 UTC.
liam_sre: action plan:
- sam_infra: continue manual validation of 3 candidate nodes and record sequence/time. (starting now)
- jordan_hw: open case with vendor with log bundle and ask for emergency hotfix or signed guidance.
- maya_oncall: be ready to rollback bmc-fw to v1.2.2 if vendor says it's safe — will need approval from infra leads.
- ops-bot: create incident ticket and add paging for any additional capacity loss.
sam_infra: started validating host 10.12.34.56 — double power-cycle cleared Boot Override after the second cycle ~2m10s, node booted into OS and joined k8s.
maya_oncall: good. what's the time per host expected if we have to do this fleet-wide manually?
sam_infra: with logistics (remote PDU latency, waiting for NVRAM rebuild) estimate ~7–9 minutes per host for a technician-driven cycle. Remote-only double-cycle with no human in loop ~4–6 minutes but needs careful pacing to avoid hitting BMC rate limits.
jordan_hw: vendor responded: they confirmed the NVRAM race. Hotfix ETA 24–36 hours. They explicitly warned against mass remote power-cycling during business hours due to PDU chain reconverge issues.
liam_sre: suggestion: prioritize canary nodes and low-impact racks first, run double-cycle procedure, monitor join rate. If vendor hotfix delayed, coordinate a staged rollback to v1.2.2 for the remaining pool — rollback plan exists but will require rolling reboots of BMC and soft power cycles.
maya_oncall: agreed. i'll coordinate with support and schedule maintenance window if rollback needed. tagging infra leads now.
sam_infra: logging manual steps for runbook and will post summary once we've completed 12 nodes of canary.
deploy-bot: Note: automated rollback option available in the deployment service for bmc-fw-v1.2.3 -> v1.2.2, requires explicit approval and will queue nodes for reflash (expected ~3h per 100 nodes including verification).
ops-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2024-1178 (west1 oob boot-override stuck after bmc-fw-v1.2.3). Added playbook link and canary checklist.
maya_oncall: thanks team. keep updates short and status-only in this thread. I'll page oncall if join rate drops below 50% of canary target.
sam_infra: will do — 12 nodes validated so far, 10 cleared with double-cycle, 2 still stuck and vendor-engaged. continuing.
